etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 了 (ryō, “comprehend”) + 承 (shō, “agree to”). 了 (“to finish”) is a daiyōji replacing 諒 (“to excuse, to forgive; to guess, to presume”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese compound 任命 (MC nyimH mjaengH, “burden, charge + command”). Compare modern Mandarin 任命 (rènmìng, “to appoint”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 売り (uri) + 出し (dashi, the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 出す (dasu))

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 投(な)げる (nageru, “to throw”) + 出(だ)す (dasu, “to send out”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
A regular shift from Classical Japanese 掲(かか)ぐ (kakagu), itself a contraction of 掻(か)き上(あ)ぐ (kakiagu, modern form 掻(か)き上(あ)げる (kakiageru)).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Formerly ゆらく (yuraku), with the final -ku softening to -gu. Derived from adverb ゆら (yura, evoking the sound of a ball or bell rocking), itself derived from or cognate with the imperfective form of Old Japanese verb ゆる (yuru) (揺る / 淘る / 汰る, "to rock, to shake").
Compare 揺れる (yureru, “to shake; to be unsettled; to hesitate”).

etymologies.text: Middle Chinese 明瞭

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 滿月 /满月 (mɑ̌n ngjwot, literally “full + moon”). Compare modern Min Nan reading móa-ge̍h.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/majo/ → /maju/
A shift from older reading 眉(まよ) (mayo) below.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. Appears in the Man'yōshū poetry anthology of the mid-700s with the reading mayo. The ma element is very likely 目(ま) (ma, “eye”, ancient combining form of modern me reading), but the derivation of the yo element is unclear.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The ma element is most likely 目(ま) (ma, “eye”, ancient combining form of modern me reading).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 眉 (MC mij).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 結(むす)ぶ (musubu).
First appears in the Man'yōshū of 759 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 花(はな) (hana, “flower”) + やか (-yaka, “seeming like”); compare English flowery.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Classical Japanese verb 訪(おとづ)る (otoduru). Analyzable as 音(おと) (oto, “sound”) + 連(つ)れる (tsureru, “to bring along; to accompany”); the tsureru changes to zureru as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the causative form of Proto-Japonic *nonk- (“to flee, escape”). Compare 逃がす (nigasu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 風車 (MC pjuwng tsyhae, “wind + wheel”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 風 (kaza, “wind”, the older combining form) + 車 (kuruma, “wheel”). The kuruma changes to guruma as an instance of rendaku (連濁).
